modes.name: Keying slip: a record filed under an ID it does not belong to
modes.summary: A structured record (export row, log entry, filed note) carries an ID that is not its owner's. The default joins on the printed key and prices, counts or routes the record under that ID. The files make that impossible: two or more first-hand remarks from different parties describe the record's content, and only the true owner fits. Fable usually notices the conflict and keeps the record anyway; Astra joins silently. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 345/680, Astra 321/670; all stages Fable 742/1835, Astra 602/1490 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 297/610, Astra 257/580. Audited GENUINE in 13 task(s). Status proven: audited GENUINE in 13 tasks; pooled final miss rate >= 0.2 with n >= 20 on fable, astra (unaudited >= 90% units excluded).

recipe.record: an official-looking keyed record (export row, dispatch line, inbox row) whose own content fits its printed key well enough to pass a casual check
recipe.anchors: two or more by-the-way remarks from different parties, each in a document read for another purpose, that describe the record's content and fit only the true owner; at least one makes the printed owner impossible (a date, a location, a transfer)
recipe.withheld: no sentence gives the key or record priority, and no sentence names the mechanism of the slip (no 'typo', no 'page-number slip'); the solver supplies the mechanism
dials: one by-the-way anchor per notch toward solvable (a witness of the event or a unique content match)
for Astra change the KIND of evidence, not the amount
never add a descriptor only the true owner has: it flips the bite to 0
recipe.conservation: when the record could be credited to both IDs, grade both sides against a conserved total so the union answer loses
recipe.shields: if a tempting rule exists, scope it away from the keyed variable explicitly

proof_obligations: uniqueness: solve.py enumerates the candidate owners and exactly one fits every anchor
ablation: dropping each anchor leaves the owner underdetermined or the default (executed)
no-priority grep: no fixture sentence binds the printed key (audits withdrew psychopathy 2.1.0, ktp 2.1.0, cafe 2.1.0 for one)
additivity: the keyed reading fails exactly this premise's checks (design_lint)
blind reader before any dial when a model misses 5/5
hazards: a sentence that blesses the record makes it AMBIGUOUS: psychopathy 2.1.0 P4 ('the log decides'), ktp 2.1.0 P2 ('the class journal records each lesson'), cafe 2.1.0 P10 (clause 2.2 'drawings govern')
two records that conflict symmetrically with nothing to decide between them: coloring 2.2.0 P2/P5/P8 AMBIGUOUS, fixed by one first-hand remark in 2.3.0
a column whose provenance is unstated while a rule defers to it: probation 2.2.0 P4 (AMBIGUOUS, re-audit UNCLEAR)
a later dated note that supports the printed label: feast 1.1.0 P3 AMBIGUOUS
a graded label that exists in no file: line-colour 1.0.0 P2 DEFECT
a 'credit both' reading left open when nothing makes the printed owner impossible: ats 1.1.0 and 1.6.0 P2, closed by an impossibility anchor in 1.7.0
often flat: 10 of the 19 audited units in the 45-task pass were missed at least 90% by Fable (kibo P3, pathway P2, ats P2, suitcase P5)
kills: one descriptor only the true owner has: cnc 2.4.0/2.5.0 P3 'still coiled, wire-tied' took 15/15 to 0/5 on both models
a specific first-hand noun: coloring 2.4.0/2.5.0 'little crow' took Fable to 2/15, 4/15, 0/15
a new note placed beside the anchor primes a destination check: gst 1.5.0 P1 11/15 to 0/5 with byte-identical premise text
one origin remark: gst 1.5.0 P4 'lorry up from Hubballi' 13/15 to 0/5
kibo 2.8.0 P3 dial (hand-typed name route) overshot to 0/5 on both
trace_signals: the user corrects which file, row, ID or person an item belongs to
two lists keyed by IDs that are easy to transpose (adjacent register lines, consecutive slide or order numbers)
a record built by someone other than the people who saw the event (data entry from paper slips, an export of hand-typed names)
modes.example: An export row keyed to a learner who transferred out three days before slips were collected carries a combination that the homeroom teacher's note and a club leader's remark both tie to a classmate whose slip is missing from the export.

modes.name: Convention fixed only by worked figures in the governing document
modes.summary: The governing text states what to compute but not how to round, count or bound it; only its worked figures (or a filed record of the same procedure) fix the convention: truncate vs half-up, which end of a range, whether the arrival day counts. The default applies the ordinary convention (round(), half-up, plain mean). This mode now covers every convention set by worked figures, as authors template it; rounding and truncation are its strongest sub-shape. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 185/970, Astra 129/950; all stages Fable 439/2670, Astra 252/2065 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 137/920, Astra 114/900. Audited GENUINE in 10 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: no model with pooled final rate >= 0.2 at n >= 20; not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

recipe.record: the governing rule states the quantity and its precision but not the convention
recipe.anchors: worked figures in the governing document itself, or in a same-procedure filed record the rule points to; for Astra exactly one discriminating figure outside the entry that defines the graded rate
recipe.withheld: no sentence names the convention ('truncate', 'cut', 'count the arrival day')
dials: the number and placement of discriminating figures: one figure gave Astra about 100% in several builds; two gave anywhere from 3/15 to 14/15
a figure inside the entry that defines the graded rate kills it for Astra
keep non-discriminating figures (both conventions agree) as cover
recipe.conservation: graded figures must discriminate under every upstream answer the solver could give (grade on the solver's own list)
recipe.shields: the task's own other content must not act as a competing example set, or the audit must show it is not governing (deck titles)

proof_obligations: discrimination: solve.py shows each plausible convention fails at least one worked figure, and exactly one fits all
placement: every worked figure sits in the governing text or a same-module filed record (eco-guard 2.1.0 fix)
additivity: the default convention fails exactly this premise's checks
census: deliverables diffed against the reference to separate convention misses from cascades
hazards: worked figures in documents the rule does not govern make it AMBIGUOUS: eco-guard 2.1.0 P3 (sheets from another year and module), brightwater 1.3.0 P3 ('within' promises outside the site-promise rule)
the idiom 'to one decimal place' reads as ordinary rounding: profile 2.1.0-2.4.0 P5 shipped GENUINE-soft
one discriminating figure is GENUINE-soft at best: deck 2.8.0 P4, gst 1.7.0 P2
a cascade from an upstream answer graded against the reference: gst 1.3.0 P2 DEFECT (convention missed 0/30 once fixed)
a token nobody can settle (a spaced em dash counted or not as a word): moot 2.1.0 P10 AMBIGUOUS
a competing example set inside the task (the deck's own v3 titles cited as precedent): deck 2.3.0 and 2.8.0 disclosures
kills: a worked figure inside the entry that defines the graded rate: profile 2.5.0 P5 Astra 14/15 to 0/5, never recovered in 2.6-2.8
figures one division away from the graded case: coloring spine 0/30 in every form
a stated precedent clause: kibo 2.1.0 P4 (5/5 to 0/5)
one figure for Fable: 18/200 misses in the 45-task pass
trace_signals: the user corrects a rounding or a count the assistant computed
a style guide or procedure with examples but no explicit rounding rule
filed earlier reports that show the house convention
modes.example: A house style gives figures over one million in millions with one decimal; its one discriminating worked example shows 2,480,000 as 2.4 million (half-up would give 2.5), so the graded figures must be cut, not rounded.

modes.name: Quantity basis cued only on or about the record (tax-inclusive, per pack)
modes.summary: A price or quantity is read on the wrong basis: a tax-inclusive bill read as net, a price per pair or pack read as per piece. The basis is cued only on or about the record itself (a cheque note, a received-goods tally, the seller's filed orders), never in a caption next to the figures. Fable misses tax-inclusive bases; per-pack pricing with a tally bites both. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 78/90, Astra 23/90; all stages Fable 153/235, Astra 49/200 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 4 task(s). Status proven: audited GENUINE in 4 tasks; pooled final miss rate >= 0.2 with n >= 20 on fable, astra (unaudited >= 90% units excluded).

recipe.record: a bill, list price or order line whose figures look complete on the default basis
recipe.anchors: a cue on the record or about this record (a tally of what was received, the seller's own filed order lines, a remark that the rise was not passed on)
recipe.withheld: no caption or column header states the basis
dials: change the kind of evidence (a received-goods tally moved Astra where more filed lists of the same kind did not: cnc 2.6.0 P4)
the weakest oblique cue restored the Fable bite on gst P3 ('same rates as our counter board')
recipe.conservation: the per-piece reading must contradict a received count or a total
recipe.shields: a 'printed rate governs' rule must be scoped to rates, not to what the price includes

proof_obligations: uniqueness: only one basis reproduces the tally or the paid total
ablation: without the on-record cue the basis is underdetermined (executed)
blind reader: a non-governing-document cue that the reader also misses is unfair
hazards: a cue in a caption next to the figures is a stated rule: suitcase 2.2.0/2.3.0 P7 Fable 0/10
a cue only in a non-governing document with one out-of-population figure: suitcase 2.4.0/2.5.0 P7, blind reader also missed (UNCONFIRMED)
a single route is GENUINE-soft: cnc 2.3.0 P4
bimodal by model: tax-inclusive bit Fable 33/40 finals and Astra 0/40 (gst P3)
kills: one extra cue on every line: gst 1.5.0/1.6.0 P3 10/15 to 1/5 and 0/5 ('a single figure on each line', a second 'nothing to add on' note)
student P3 tax-exclusive quote: 0/15 F, 0/10 A

receipts or tallies that disagree with list prices

modes.example: A bearing listed at one price per line is ordered one per piece, though the seller's own filed orders and the receiving tally show each line delivered two pieces.

modes.name: Already in hand: a 'still needed' item already held, shown by a technical bridge
modes.summary: A rule orders or chases what is still needed, and a list says an item is outstanding. A first-hand record shows the item is already held, through a technical bridge the solver must make (a controller already running a known board; a vendor's job sheet for the scanned specimen). The default orders or chases the item. It dies when possession is stated. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 13/70, Astra 8/70; all stages Fable 24/165, Astra 13/145 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 2 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: no model with pooled final rate >= 0.2 at n >= 20; not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

recipe.record: a still-needed list or chase line that names the item as outstanding
recipe.anchors: two first-hand records whose technical content shows the item is held (a log line, a job sheet, an adviser's identification of the object)
recipe.withheld: no sentence says the item arrived or is owned
dials: one semantic bridge per notch; two bridges were disclosed as the soft point in cnc 2.6.0
recipe.conservation: grade the order or chase list as an exact set
recipe.shields: scope any 'chase everything on the list' rule to items not yet received

proof_obligations: uniqueness: exactly one listed item is shown held
ablation: each bridge anchor is necessary (executed)
no-statement grep: no line states possession
hazards: two semantic bridges were disclosed as the soft point: cnc 2.6.0 P5
measured on two tasks only: cnc P5 (Fable) and psychopathy 2.4.0 P6 (Astra, templated T4 by its author)
kills: possession stated outright: kibo 2.5.0/2.6.0 P5 commander scope, Fable 0/10

brightwater 1.4.0-1.6.0 P5 (T4 build): Fable 0/20 finals

modes.name: Misfiled note or record: filed under one item, content only fits another
modes.summary: A note, comment, letter or certificate is filed under item A, but what it says can only be about item B (dates, details or a description that A cannot meet). The default applies it to A as filed. Content-only misfiles bit Astra hard in some builds (ats, pathway) and not at all in others (spice 2.5.0, line-colour 1.4.0, timesheet 2.7.0). Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 26/80, Astra 41/80; all stages Fable 53/170, Astra 81/170 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 26/60, Astra 21/60. Audited GENUINE in 2 task(s). Status proven: audited GENUINE in 2 tasks; pooled final miss rate >= 0.2 with n >= 20 on fable, astra (unaudited >= 90% units excluded).

recipe.record: a complete note or comment that fits its filed key on a casual read
recipe.anchors: two near-true details in the note that A cannot meet and B does (a date offset, a prior history), each checked against a record read for another purpose
recipe.withheld: no sentence says the note was misfiled
dials: two near-true details: the ats 1.6.0 reader solved it, models still missed
an impossibility on A closes the 'apply to both' reading
recipe.conservation: grade both A's and B's resulting values so 'apply to both' loses
recipe.shields: none needed unless a filing rule exists; then scope it

proof_obligations: uniqueness: only B meets every detail of the note
ablation: each detail is necessary
both-side grading: the union answer fails a check
hazards: an instruction-like note admitting a second destination: deck 2.5.0 N5 AMBIGUOUS (fixed 2.6.0)

spice 2.5.0 P7 and line-colour 1.4.0 P5: 0/5 on both

modes.name: Which edition or rate applies, by the real date (sources of similar authority)
modes.summary: Two editions, briefs or rates could govern; the log's key or date points to one, and first-hand dated records show the request really arrived under the other. The default trusts the log's date or the newest edition. It bites both models when the competing sources have similar authority; it is unfair when an informal remark contradicts an official printed form. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 50/80, Astra 78/90; all stages Fable 96/245, Astra 113/140 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded); without unaudited >=90% units, final Fable 50/80, Astra 59/70. Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). Status promising: short of proven: audited GENUINE in 1 task(s) (< 2); not dead (some model above 0.05 or n < 20).

recipe.anchors: first-hand dated records (a fitting date, a recording made on a named day) that place the real receipt in the other edition's window
recipe.withheld: no mapping rule from date to edition is stated
dials: one oblique sentence moved cafe P1/P6 into the band on Fable ('on Thursday')

modes.name: Convention from two worked figures supplied by different parties
modes.summary: A convention (build at the floor, not at the nominal height) is shown by two worked figures from two different parties, one in a standard and one in a client's filed request. The default applies the nominal reading. Measured on one task only. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 9/30, Astra 4/40; all stages Fable 16/55, Astra 7/55 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). recipe.withheld: the convention is never stated
dials: a third figure moves it toward solvable

recipe.shields: scope any 'nominal heights govern' sentence

modes.name: Changed premise received before issue (filler only)
modes.summary: A letter received before the issue date changes a premise (a door must stay an escape door), so verdicts computed on the old premise are wrong. The default keeps the earlier verdicts. Measured on one task; the catalogue keeps it as a filler. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 7/30, Astra 0/40; all stages Fable 12/55, Astra 0/55 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). recipe.withheld: no instruction says to re-check

modes.name: Rule-scope shield: a real rule on a neighbouring value over-applied
modes.summary: A real rule governs a neighbouring value (a guide section that leaves late sitters out of the gain); the default over-applies it to the graded value (it also leaves their pre-test out). Three or more lines show the graded value stands. Fable cites the rule; Astra rarely misses. Measured here (build_evidence.py, 2026-10-15): final 10x2 pooled Fable 32/60, Astra 3/60; all stages Fable 55/120, Astra 4/120 (AMBIGUOUS/DEFECT units excluded). Audited GENUINE in 1 task(s). modes.name: Structural misfile: a one-row-per file with a second row for the same key
modes.summary: A file holds one row (comment, line) per item and says so; the filed key already has its own row, a second row under that key quotes another item's content, and the true item has no row. modes.name: A by-design irregularity 'corrected' (re-normalised shares, fixed base)
modes.summary: Default: after computing correctly, the agent 'repairs' a figure that looks wrong by textbook standards: it re-normalises shares that sum to less than 100%, recomputes a contracted fixed base on actuals, or closes a deliberate residual. recipe.record: A cost-sharing schedule whose tenant shares sum to 96% (the landlord bears 4% for a vacant unit), or a hotel block contract priced on a fixed 1,200 contracted room-nights.
recipe.anchors: (1) Last year's worked apportionment statement in the governing agreement (party A, the managing agent) whose charges reproduce only without re-normalising. modes.name: Additive local layer read as an override of the base schedule
modes.summary: Default: when a base schedule and a same-named local layer (a site, region, package or project file with the same title, columns and item names) both carry an entry for one item, the agent keeps one entry, usually letting the later or more specific layer override the base, and drops the other. The files make that wrong because the layers add: a governing entitlement from another party guarantees the base entry to everyone in scope, so the override reading breaches it, and a different party's worked line items show both elements paid together; nothing says how the layers combine. Trace support is essentially ONE session (01a0ce05: the user corrected that same-named files across packages are cumulative after the assistant had let the later package's duplicates win); 01a0d332 is weaker support (a security verdict that turned on how a project-level file combines with global settings, and the first pass dropped that layer). aimed_at both is an expectation, not a measurement: Fable's newest/most-specific default and Astra's silent keyed join (last write wins) both keep one layer. Not measured here; pilot first.

recipe.record: A local-layer schedule with the same title, columns and item names as the base schedule, later dated and more specific (site, region, package or project), carrying an entry for the item the deliverable prices; read alone it looks like a complete restatement of the base.
recipe.anchors: (1) A governing document of another party (collective agreement, master contract, group policy) guarantees the base entry to everyone in scope, so reading the local entry as a replacement breaches it for the affected item. (2) A different party's worked line items for one comparable case (payroll bureau payslip extract, carrier invoice, insurer's premium breakdown) show the base and local elements as two lines. (3) Optional: the local owner's budget note costs only the local element, named by description, never by a figure a script can match.
recipe.withheld: No 'in addition', 'top-up', 'supplement', 'replaces' or 'supersedes' wording in any title, header or note; no sentence on how layers combine; the mechanism (a local element paid on top of the base) is supplied by the model.
dials: the entitlement anchor is the strong notch: pilot with it and the worked line items only
for Astra change the kind of evidence (a cost-centre ledger split) rather than adding another remark
a local entry smaller than the guaranteed base makes override impossible; a larger one only makes it implausible: choose deliberately and record which
keep the affected population small: one to three items that appear in both layers
recipe.conservation: Grade the per-item total and its split by payer or cost centre (base vs local), so keeping one layer, booking the sum under one payer, or counting the local entry twice each misses.
recipe.shields: A real precedence rule scoped to a neighbouring item (site schedules replace group rates for overtime, say); Fable may cite it, and the audit must show its grammar does not reach the trapped item.

proof_obligations: uniqueness: only base plus local satisfies every anchor; override, base-only and double counting each break one
consistency: every item present in both layers combines the same way; no overlapping item supports the override reading
ablation: dropping the entitlement anchor leaves the worked line items deciding; dropping both leaves the item undecided, and the validator reports it
executed counterfactual: the override reading produces a different deliverable on every check routed through the item
census of wrong answers: override, base-only, sum under one payer and local counted twice each fail at least one graded check
no anomaly under the default: the override reading leaves no unmatched row or missing value
blind reader reaches the additive reading with no sentence stating how layers combine
hazards: Real layering conventions differ (configuration files override; tariffs and allowances often add): built on file structure alone the item is ambiguous, so the entitlement or worked-line anchor is mandatory
With a worked figure as the only anchor this is T7 (a convention from two parties' worked figures), not R1
Inverse of L11 (one event under two document numbers counted twice): never route both through one pair of schedules in a task
Base-only items must still price under the override default, or the gap is an anomaly the agent's own script finds
01a0ce05 is a data-extraction session rejected as requires_execution: the mechanism transfers, the fixture must be a written schedule a reader can check
kills: a title, header or note calling the local file a supplement, top-up or replacement (a stated rule, D1)
a sentence saying local entries are paid in addition to, or instead of, base entries
a worked line labelled with the local file's name beside the trapped item
trace_signals: the user says same-named files or schedules across packages, sites or versions are cumulative, not alternatives
the assistant resolved duplicate entries by letting the later or more specific source win
a verdict depends on how a project-level or local file combines with global settings
domains: written reviews of layered policy or configuration settings
modes.example: A group allowance schedule and a site schedule both list a remote-shift meal allowance per grade under the same name. The collective agreement guarantees the group allowance to all staff, and the payroll bureau's payslip extract for another site worker shows two meal lines. Deliverable: a per-worker monthly allowance register with the group and site cost-centre totals.

modes.name: Planned quantity exceeds a capacity fixed only by other parties' facts
modes.summary: Default: the agent derives a plan quantity top-down from the principal's driver (leads times conversion rates, a compressed timeline, a target volume) and carries it into the schedule without checking the supply side. The files make that wrong because routine documents from two other parties (a clinician's rota and the receptionist's slot length; a teaching timetable and the field plan's visit lengths) fix a capacity the plan cannot exceed; no document states the capacity as a number or says the target is infeasible. Seen in TWO sessions: 01a0c97e (monthly evaluation targets one professional could not see) and 01a0d157 (a one-year fieldwork plan infeasible for teaching lecturers); both assistants conceded once the user objected. Kin to L9 (the work order presupposes a feasible target) and D3 (stored figure vs derivation, dead): stating the capacity turns it into D3. aimed_at both is an expectation: Astra applies the top-down default silently, Fable tends to add a caveat and keep the target (01a0c97e's assistant said its caveat came after the numbers). Not measured here; pilot first.

recipe.record: The principal's plan or KPI sheet (a dated folder document, never the task instruction) states the target volume or schedule, derived top-down and internally consistent; the deliverable carries it into a dated plan.
recipe.anchors: (1) A second party's routine operating document fixes the supply side by structure, not by a capacity figure (a rota listing the sessions the clinician holds for evaluations; a timetable showing teaching weeks). (2) A third party's routine record fixes what each item consumes, by description (the receptionist's handbook: one evaluation fills one session slot of a stated length; the field plan: each site visit takes a stated span of days). (3) Optional notch: a by-the-way remark that the sessions are already full, or that teaching blocks travel.
recipe.withheld: No sentence states the capacity as a number, says the target exceeds it, or ranks the target against the rota; the governing text states only the positive general rule (evaluations are booked into the clinician's evaluation sessions; fieldwork happens outside teaching weeks).
dials: each extra witness of the limit (a full diary export, a cancelled-visit note) is one notch toward solvable
printing the capacity as a figure anywhere is a large notch and turns the premise into D3 (dead)
for Astra change the kind of evidence (a booking export) rather than adding a remark
keep the capped population small: one or two weeks or phases where the plan exceeds the limit
recipe.conservation: Grade the capped quantity and a downstream figure only the capped plan reconciles (leads to contact, attendances expected, travel budget), so booking the target with a caveat, or capping without carrying it downstream, misses.
recipe.shields: A real growth or minimum-volume rule scoped to another quantity (a marketing lead-volume commitment, a funder's minimum output count), which Fable may cite to keep the target.

proof_obligations: uniqueness: the anchors fix exactly one capacity under every reading of the rota and slot length, and the target lies outside it by a wide margin
ablation: dropping either structural anchor leaves the capacity undetermined; the validator shows both are needed
executed counterfactual: the uncapped plan yields a different deliverable on every check routed through the cap
census of wrong answers: the target, the target with a caveat, a cap from one anchor, and the cap without downstream changes each fail a graded check
no anomaly under the default: the uncapped plan leaves no overbooked slot, unmatched row or stated total in the deliverable
blind reader caps the plan with no sentence that states the capacity
hazards: If the task's principal binds the target ('book the KPI') and nothing makes the supply-side rule govern, a blind reader keeps the target: unfair. The booking rule must be a real, positive SOP sentence
If the deliverable assigns individual slots or dates, the default overbooks visibly and the agent's own check finds it; grade weekly or phase totals
A limit known only from general knowledge (boiling points, statutory hours) must be supplied by a party in the folder; otherwise the rule has a missing input (an audit-rejected shape)
Do not route an L9 presupposition and this cap through the same item
01a0c6d5 looked like this mode (runs set above a co-solvent's boiling point) but used sealed reactors, where that is routine: a limit that holds for one vessel type is T9 territory, not R2
kills: a stated capacity figure (slots per week, person-days available)
a field or question asking whether the plan is feasible
a remark that the target was set before the rota or timetable was known
trace_signals: the user says the plan is impossible for the people or equipment available
targets derived from conversion ratios or desired outputs with no supply-side check
the assistant concedes it set figures before knowing the capacity
modes.example: A clinic manager's KPI sheet derives monthly new-patient evaluations from lead volume and conversion rates. The dentist's rota holds evaluation sessions on two afternoons, one of them in alternate weeks only; the receptionist's handbook says each evaluation fills one session slot of a stated length. Deliverable: next month's weekly evaluation bookings, leads to contact and expected attendances.
